habitat: Pairs, mostly in thornveld, in the lower stratum. Newman says it is most common in arid western regions.
summary: A common near-endemic resident. Black above with a white wing-stripe, and entirely scarlet below. A rare form has bright yellow underparts. Very young birds are ash-grey below, finely barred black. The birds duet a sharp qui-quip-chiri. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Boubou is black above with a white wing-bar, but the underparts grade from a white throat to a cinnamon belly, not scarlet.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 16–64.

underparts.pattern: Entirely scarlet underparts. The colour line says crimson. A rare form has bright yellow underparts. Scarlet, crimson and that yellow form are not stored as a single token.

research.note: Newman calls it a common near-endemic resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged. Scarlet and crimson are not colour tokens, so the underpart colour is left blank and described in the pattern. The rare yellow form is noted and not given its own variant.
